subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser SSRF private-network confirmation/grant mode, and what permanent policy shape should cover approvals, allow/block lists, hard metadata endpoints, and temporary grants?
rationale: Current source proves the gap exists, but this would add public config and user-approval semantics for a security-sensitive private-network boundary that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design Browser SSRF Policy First
options.body: Keep this open while maintainers define one browser-owned approval and allow/block contract before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Policy
options.body: Treat confirmation and allow/block lists as part of a broader network egress policy design that also covers related web_fetch and domain-denylist requests.

options.title: Keep Existing Explicit Opt-In Only
options.body: Decline confirmation mode for now and document that users must choose strict blocking, exact host exceptions, or dangerous private-network opt-in.

recommendation.title: Design Browser SSRF Policy First
recommendation.body: Keep this open while maintainers define one browser-owned approval and allow/block contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The sampled history and recent related merges most strongly route browser SSRF/security-boundary decisions through this owner signal.
